recipe_title: Citrus and Pistachio Shaved Brussels Sprouts Slaw

details.title_candidate: Citrus and Pistachio Shaved Brussels Sprouts Slaw

warnings: [ingredient_instruction_consistency] There is a minor redundancy. The ingredients list specifies '1 oz (30 g) Shelled pistachios (roughly chopped)', but step 5 instructs the reader to 'Chop the pistachios roughly.' Fix: Either list them whole and have the reader chop them in step 5, or keep them chopped in the ingredients and remove step 5.

details.summary: A superb, highly practical recipe that hits every nutritional and culinary target for the book. Aside from a minor instruction redundancy regarding chopping the pistachios, this no-cook slaw is ready for print.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent. The bitterness of the Brussels sprouts is perfectly balanced by the sweetness and acidity of the orange and apple cider vinegar, while the olive oil and pistachios provide grounding richness.

There is a minor redundancy. The ingredients list specifies '1 oz (30 g) Shelled pistachios (roughly chopped)', but step 5 instructs the reader to 'Chop the pistachios roughly.' Fix: Either list them whole and have the reader chop them in step 5, or keep them chopped in the ingredients and remove step 5.
The instructions are clear and practical. The cue to 'massage lightly... to soften' the Brussels sprouts is exactly what a home cook needs to know to make a raw sprout salad work.
Perfectly aligns with Modern American cuisine, where shaved Brussels sprout salads with fruit and nuts are a staple.
The no-cook method is ideal for these ingredients. Massaging the slaw is the correct technique for raw Brussels sprouts.
The macro calculations are highly accurate for the stated ingredients. The calorie, carbohydrate, and fat counts perfectly reflect the oil, nuts, orange, and sprouts.
The title accurately describes the dish, and the intro is practical, encouraging, and free of any banned health claims.
Highly appealing. It's a vibrant, texturally interesting, and refreshing dish that feels elevated but takes almost no time to make.
An exemplary recipe for this dietary profile. It provides a massive 7.1g of fiber, uses heart-healthy unsaturated fats (olive oil and pistachios), and centers on whole vegetables and fruit.

Perfectly executed. Added sugar is genuinely zero, utilizing the whole fresh orange to provide all the necessary sweetness. The carbohydrate component (21.2g) sits right in the optimal window and comes entirely from high-quality, high-fiber whole foods.

Fits the 'Snacks & Sides' chapter nicely. While categorized as a snack (and it works as a large, filling one), it also functions beautifully as one of the simple slaws promised in the chapter's 'Sides' intro.
Extremely practical. Utilizing pre-bagged shaved Brussels sprouts is a fantastic, accessible supermarket shortcut that keeps the active time well under the 10-minute mark.
